title: Errors and retries
description: Recover from temporary failures without duplicating jobs.

sections.title: Read status and message
paragraphs: API errors use a simple object such as {"error":"job capacity reached"}. Branch primarily on HTTP status; do not expect nested error.code values. Conversion failures are reported on a successful job-status response.

sections.title: Retry deliberately
table: Correct the input or server capabilities.
Check the ID, owner, and expiration.
Poll the job before retrying download or deletion.
Wait with bounded exponential backoff and jitter.
Retry reads with a deadline; avoid blindly repeating uploads.

sections.title: Avoid duplicate creation
paragraphs: POST /v1/jobs has no idempotency key. A timeout may occur after a job was accepted. Do not automatically resend an upload after an ambiguous response. Keep any returned job ID.
sections.code:
const delayMs = Math.min(1000 * 2 ** attempt, 10000);
await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, delayMs + Math.random() * 250));

sections.title: A job failure is different from an HTTP failure
paragraphs: A status request can return 200 while the job is failed. Inspect job.status and job.error even after response.ok is true. conversion_failed means the worker failed or exceeded its timeout; conversion_interrupted indicates a durable job was running when the service restarted.

Do not repeatedly retry malformed or unsupported files. Inspect the input and installed engine first. If an infrastructure interruption caused the failure, a new submission can be appropriate after the service is healthy.

sections.title: Bound retries by count and time
paragraphs: Use a small maximum number of attempts and an overall deadline. Jitter prevents many clients from retrying at the same instant. Stop immediately on authentication or validation errors and surface a useful message to the caller.
The SDK does not automatically retry HTTP failures. A higher-level application can wrap safe read operations with backoff. Treat ambiguous upload failures separately because POST is not idempotent.
